subject: SIG follow-up: audit-log preservation & evidence delivery for legal hold
messages:
From: Aurelia Turner <aurelia.turner@finserv.com>

Cc: LegalOps <legalops@finserv.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: legal hold preservation + signed export (SIG follow-up)

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this — we're finalizing a SIG for our internal auditors and need to confirm Redwood's capability to preserve and deliver audit logs under a legal hold. High level asks:

- Can you place a tenant-level hold (prevent deletion/retention truncation) for a specified time window?
- If we request an export, what is the typical turnaround and delivery mechanism (S3 presigned URL, direct push to our S3, or downloadable bundle)?
- What export formats do you provide (JSONL, CSV, Parquet) and do you include a signed manifest with per-file checksums for chain-of-custody?
- Do you provide an operator/audit trail showing who requested/approved the export and timestamps?
- We also need guidance on how long Redwood will retain the snapshot after providing it and options to extend holds.

Regulatory context: this is for a potential SEC/FINRA request — may need immutable evidence retention and a clear chain-of-custody.

Please include any sample artifacts or manifests we can attach to the SIG response.

Best,
Aurelia Turner
Senior Legal Ops
FinServ Bank

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Aurelia Turner <aurelia.turner@finserv.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: legal hold preservation + signed export (SIG follow-up)

Aurelia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Monica (Security) and Grace (Customer Ops) to confirm technical and operational details. A few quick clarifying questions so we scope it correctly:

1) Do you need us to *freeze* deletion for the live tenant (prevent future background retention trimming) or do you only need a one-time immutable export for a date range?
2) What timeliness SLA do auditors expect for an export request (48h, 72h, longer)?
3) Any PII/PII-redaction preferences (full PII included in the export vs. redacted/stubs)?

Proposed starting approach: produce an immutable snapshot (export) for the requested window, deliver via a KMS-encrypted gzipped JSONL bundle, and include a signed manifest with SHA256 per-file plus a chain-of-custody CSV. Monica — can you outline the mechanics? Grace — I'll coordinate the MAP and timeline with Aurelia once we have the tech details.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Customer Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aurelia Turner <aurelia.turner@finserv.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: legal hold preservation + signed export (SIG follow-up)

Hi Aurelia — thanks, Mark. Technical summary and delivery options below. I'll keep this high-level for the SIG but can provide a sample export and manifest (attached) for evidence.

What Redwood can do today:
- Tenant hold: we can set a tenant-level retention hold which prevents automated deletion and retention truncation for up to the requested hold period. This toggles a retention flag and extends lifecycle policies; hold requests are recorded in our operator audit log.
- Exports: we create a snapshot export for a specified time range. Default format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL), gzipped. Optionally we can produce CSV or Parquet on request for larger, structured event sets.
- Chain-of-custody: every export includes:
  - a signed manifest file (ASCII text) listing filenames, file sizes, and SHA256 checksums
  - a separate operator-audit CSV that logs the export job ID, requesting principal, approver (if configured), start/end timestamps, and Redwoods's artifact signing certificate serial
  - an internal action log export showing any retention hold changes for the tenant during the timeframe.
- Delivery options:
  - S3 presigned URL to a Redwood-managed bucket (default) — URLs valid for 7 days.
  - Push to customer's S3 bucket (requires cross-account role/trust; we can create a short-lived role for the export job).
  - Secure transfer via our support channel (for highly restricted accounts).
- Encryption & integrity:
  - Artifacts are KMS-encrypted at rest (customer-managed KMS supported for private deployments).
  - Manifest is signed by our artifact-signing key (we include the signature block and certificate fingerprint).
- Retention after delivery:
  - By default we keep the snapshot for 14 days after delivery in our archive to allow re-downloads; we can extend to 60/180/indefinite by request (this is a policy change and we log it).
- Timeline & runbook:
  - Standard SLA: 48–72 business hours for a 30-day window export. Larger windows or higher throughput tenants may take longer. Expedited (24–48h) is possible for high-priority legal holds.
  - We follow a documented playbook (attached) for legal-hold exports that includes steps for signing manifests, upload verification, and delivery confirmation.

Attachables I've included for your review: sample export (1k events truncated), sample manifest, and the legal-hold playbook. These are redacted examples (no customer data).

Questions for you so we can finalize the MAP:
- Confirm the date range you want preserved/exported.
- Do you want the tenant hold toggled (prevent future deletion) in addition to the export? If yes, for how long?
- Delivery preference: presigned URL vs push to your S3?

I'll stand by to execute once we have answers.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Security Engineer, Evidence & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: export-sample-20270421.jsonl.gz (sample), audit-manifest-20270421.txt (sample), legal-hold-playbook-Redwood.pdf

From: LegalOps <legalops@finserv.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: legal hold preservation + signed export (SIG follow-up)

Thanks Monica — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Regulatory scope: SEC/FINRA and EU Data Protection (possible cross-border considerations). We will need the exported manifest to contain per-file SHA256 and a manifest signature that we can verify.
- PII: for the SIG we prefer to show that PII is preserved and handled; we do not need raw PII in the sample artifact — redacted sample is fine. For the actual legal hold export, auditors will request full fidelity (including PII), so ensure your process supports that under secure delivery.
- SLA & cost: can Redwood commit to a 72-hour max for initial delivery for a typical 90-day export window? Also confirm if this is considered a billable special operation or covered under our entitlements — we would prefer no unexpected charges.

Please send the sample manifest and a short MAP (steps + owners + target dates).

Regards,
Legal Ops Team
FinServ Bank
